User Guide & Feature Manual - Online Edition

Welcome to the Project Tracker. This intuitive, single-page application is designed to simplify project scheduling, Gantt chart visualization, and automated progress reporting. Below is a quick, efficient guide to help you master every feature in the app.

Profiles, GitHub & Offline Recovery

Browser saving, GitHub synchronization, JSON-file writing and offline application caching are different features. Saved locally does not mean uploaded. Wait for Synced before relying on another device having your latest work.

WhatReally cloud-synced?Where it stays
Profile names, projects, tasks, To Dos, calendar events, sound and wrap-up settingsYes, while connected and after a successful uploadYour private GitHub repository, with a working copy in each connected browser
Pending offline editsNot until this device reconnects and uploads themThis browser; closing the page stops uploads until it is reopened
GitHub tokenNoThis browser's localStorage until Disconnect or clearing site data; never in JSON backups, linked files or the public application
Selected profile/project/date, Calendar Month/Week/layers/filters, zoom, panel sizes and collapsed branchesNoThis browser only. Calendar choices are separate per profile; folding is separate per profile/project, including after reload
Recovery snapshotsNoThis browser; included in Backup all profiles. Restoring creates a new profile that can then sync
Auto-save to JSON fileNo live file syncA one-way copy to a file on this device. Each profile has its own link; reconnect the link after reopening
Offline application cacheNo project-data syncOnly the public application page, so it can reopen offline. GitHub API responses and tokens are never put in this cache
  • Profiles: Use the dropdown to switch workspaces and the people icon to Add, Use, Rename or Delete. Profiles are not logins: a token with access to the private repository can access all its profiles.
  • GitHub connection: Paste a fine-grained token limited to one private data repository with Contents: read/write. GitHub identifies its account and repository; your website can be hosted by a different account. Each browser needs its own first connection, then remembers the token until Disconnect.
  • Automatic checks: Unless paused, uploads normally start about two seconds after editing stops. Checks also run on reopening, returning to the tab, reconnecting and every 30 seconds while visible. New profiles are discovered; existing clean inactive profiles refresh when selected. This is not instantaneous live collaboration.
  • Pause sync: Open GitHub settings > Pause sync to stop automatic checks and uploads without forgetting the token. Browser saving and enabled local JSON writing continue. The pause applies to all profiles on this browser's connection, survives closing/reloading, and does not pause other devices. A request already underway finishes safely, but queued requests wait. Use Resume sync in the same settings to check GitHub before uploading: unchanged cloud data needs no choice; divergent edits still use the normal conflict choices. Existing rate-limit waits and sync errors are not bypassed by Resume.
  • Another device: An unchanged cached profile accepts newer cloud data automatically. If only this device changed, it uploads. If both sides changed into different versions, Needs attention asks what to keep; saved offline work is not silently discarded. Checks use the last-synced version, not whichever device opened last.
  • Conflict choices: Keep this device's version uploads this copy and snapshots the previous GitHub version locally. Use GitHub's version snapshots this copy locally before loading the cloud version. Keep both keeps the cloud original and makes a separate recovered-local profile. Conflicts are per whole profile, not automatically merged task by task.
  • Busy editors: Incoming replacements wait while an editor, dialog, file chooser or drag is active. Cloud update waiting is not an error. Finishing a local edit may require a conflict choice if GitHub also changed.
  • Toolbar groups: Backups and Recovery are together; GitHub settings and its save status are together; JSON auto-save and the small offline dot are together. Help is separate. The GitHub logo opens settings, and the status SVG shows syncing or a checked cloud when synced.
  • Offline: Hover over the small dot beside JSON auto-save and wait for Offline ready before depending on offline reopening. The dot reports the cached application copy, not GitHub data sync or whether JSON writing is enabled. Only data already cached on this browser is available offline; another device cannot receive your pending edits while this page is closed or disconnected.
  • Privacy and recovery: Browser storage is not encrypted. Scripts on the same origin can read it; a /tracker/ folder shares its origin with the main website, while a separate subdomain isolates it. Clearing site data removes local tokens, views, pending edits and recovery snapshots. Keep private backups.
  • Editing tabs: One editing tab is allowed per browser origin. This does not lock a second physical device out of editing; concurrent divergent work uses the conflict choices above.

1. Project Workspace Management

Creating, Renaming & Deleting Projects

  • Create: Click the + button next to "Project Tracker" in the sidebar header to initialize a new project.
  • Rename: Hover over the project name in the sidebar and click the pencil icon, or click the project's title in the main header.
  • Delete: Hover over the project row in the sidebar and click the trash icon to permanently delete it.

Dynamic Views

Toggle between views beside the project name in the header toolbar:

  • Gantt View: Standard interactive timeline layout with editable columns.
  • Summary View: Clean, formatted textual breakdown of all tasks with progress markers—ideal for progress presentations.
  • Overview (Dashboard): Click "Overview" in the sidebar to view a high-level dashboard of all active projects, overall completion rates, and active timelines.
  • Calendar: Above To Do in the sidebar. Month and Week show this profile's To Dos, Gantt task spans and independent events together or separately.

2. Managing Tasks and Hierarchy

Building a Task Tree

Tasks can be indented to create a parent-child relationship.

  • Add Subtasks: Hover over a task and click the green + icon to add a nested subtask.
  • Indent / Outdent: Click the < or > buttons in the task's hover menu to adjust hierarchy levels.
  • Automatic Parent Tracking: Parent tasks automatically adjust their start date, duration, and completion progress based on their children, unless their progress has a manual override. Linked To Do completion can explicitly create that override; see section 6.
  • Collapse a branch: The chevron beside a parent hides or reveals all its descendants in Gantt and Summary. A collapsed parent shows how many tasks are hidden. Hidden tasks still contribute to dates, durations and progress; moving a parent still moves its complete branch.
  • Collapse / expand all: The Subtasks menu affects only the selected project. Both views share that project's folding preferences in this browser, including after reload. These preferences are not cloud-synced and do not create GitHub commits.

Progress Tracking

  • Click on any task's percentage value (e.g., 0%) to set manual progress.
  • Tip: Clear the percentage input box to revert the task (or parent) to automatic calculation mode.

Modifying and Duplicating

  • Duplicate Branch: Click the duplicate icon (overlapping squares) to copy a task and all of its subtasks instantly.
  • Rich Text Details: Double-click any task bar, or click the details folder icon to open the description editor. You can format notes, create bullet lists, and safely paste external documentation.

3. Interactive Gantt Timeline

Phones and touch screens

The interface adapts automatically to a narrow browser window, or a medium-sized touch-first screen, including phone landscape. Wide desktop windows keep the original layout and mouse controls. No PWA or home-screen installation is required.

  • Profiles and projects: The three-line button opens a drawer with a full-width profile selector, profile management, Projects, Overview and To Do. Selecting a profile or view closes the drawer.
  • Two-row project header: The first row shows the project name, separate save-status indicator and More button. Tap the project name for start-date editing and project actions, including notes. The second row combines Tasks / Timeline / Summary and View options. To Do and Overview need only the first row.
  • More: Open the three-dot header button for Backups, Recovery when available, GitHub settings, JSON auto-save and Help. JSON keeps its explicit ON / OFF label and adjacent offline dot; tap the dot for storage details. Conflicts and errors retain visible messages and a directly tappable warning.
  • View options: The sliders button contains Subtasks and Calendar / Working days. Timeline also offers Day / Week / Month zoom and Move / resize. Calendar / Working days changes only the displayed duration; the duration editor always uses calendar days.
  • Tasks / Timeline / Summary: Switch directly between full-width task cards, the scrollable chart and the project summary. Tap a task name or its three-dot actions button for notes, progress, hierarchy, branch ordering, dates, duplication and deletion.
  • Safe touch scheduling: Timeline starts in browsing mode, so swiping scrolls without changing dates. In View options, choose Move / resize to drag bars and their right edges; choose Browse / scroll afterward. An amber dot on Timeline marks editing mode. Cancellation or changing layouts discards an unfinished drag. Moving or reordering a parent includes hidden descendants.
  • To Do: Tap an item's three-dot button for editing, moving, copying, ordering, calendar export and deletion. Export the selected day and Overdue items from More > Backups.
  • Same data and exports: Rotation does not submit or discard open editors. Task/Timeline choice is browser-local, not cloud-synced. Chart exports retain their desktop report layout, not a cropped phone screen.

Timeline Navigation

Use the Day / Week / Month View menu in the header to scale your timeline. It uses the same compact popup design as Subtasks. Within an open menu, arrow keys move between available actions, Enter chooses one, and Escape closes the menu.

Drag-and-Drop Scheduling

  • Move / Reschedule: Click and hold any task bar or milestone diamond, then drag it horizontally. If you drag a parent task, all of its nested children will shift in unison.
  • Resize Duration: Hover over the right edge of any non-parent task bar until your cursor changes to a horizontal resize arrow, then drag to extend or shorten the duration.
  • Milestones: To create a milestone, append an asterisk (*) to a task's name (e.g., Launch Phase*). This converts the bar into a purple milestone diamond with a duration of 0 days.

4. Saving and State Persistence

These saving mechanisms can run together; none is a separate profile login:

A. Browser LocalStorage (Automatic)

Saved actions and local view preferences survive refreshes in this browser. Unsynced edits cannot reach another device until uploaded. Text not yet submitted in an editor or add-item field is not a saved action.

B. GitHub Cloud Sync

Connect once per browser. Synced is a read-only indicator; GitHub settings manages the connection. Temporary network failures retry; expired tokens or denied permissions need attention. Closing the page stops its synchronization. Local JSON writing is independent.

C. Auto-save to JSON file

For an additional, continuously updated copy on this device:

  1. Click Auto-save to JSON file: OFF in the main header.
  2. Your browser will prompt you to create or link a file (e.g., My_Tracker_Live.json).
  3. Once enabled, the button shows ON; hover over it to see the linked filename. Saved changes in this profile are written there. Click again to stop; neither linking nor a write failure disconnects GitHub.
  4. Re-enable the link after reopening. The file remains on disk. This is one-way writing: external file edits are not read back. Import any existing file contents you need before choosing that file for automatic writing.

Automatic writing requires this browser's file-picker support and, on the website, HTTPS. Support varies by browser and device; the app checks the actual feature rather than assuming all phones behave alike. If unavailable, browser saving, offline editing, GitHub sync and manual JSON downloads remain available.

D. Manual Backups (Import / Export)

  • Export Backup: Use Backups > Export Backup for the active profile, or Backup all profiles for every profile and its recovery snapshots. JSON always contains all tasks, including collapsed subtasks; it does not contain browser-only view preferences or the token.
  • Import Backup: Select the source and destination profile. Import as a new profile, add to existing content, or explicitly replace it. Existing destinations are backed up to Recovery first.

Manage profiles: The people icon beside the profile selector opens Add, Use, Rename and Delete. Deletion syncs to all devices and retains each device's latest local copy in its Recovery, including pending edits. It does not erase local JSON files or Git history. Recovery restores a new profile; the deleted identity is not reintroduced. Deleting the last profile creates an empty Default profile. Older apps may need updating after the first synced deletion.

GitHub connection: Your token is remembered in this browser until Disconnect, so reopening restores synchronization. It is never included in data backups. Use a trusted browser because scripts on the same website can access its stored token.

5. Exporting Assets

Generate instant stakeholder reports from the top-right header toolbar:

  • Gantt PNG image: Use Backups > Export image in Gantt view. It includes the displayed branches, not collapsed descendants, across the rendered rows rather than just the scroll viewport.
  • PDF report: Available from Backups in Gantt and Summary. It always includes every task, all notes and a fully expanded Gantt chart, regardless of folding. Your local collapsed view is restored after export.
  • Summary Copy: Copies the currently displayed summary branches. Use PDF or JSON when you need all hidden descendants as well.

6. Calendar: Month and Week

Open Calendar above To Do. It is another view of the active profile, not copied tasks or an external calendar service. Weeks run Monday to Sunday. This version is date-based: no hourly grid, recurrence or calendar drag-to-reschedule.

  • Layers: Open Settings beside Today and check To Dos, Projects and Events independently. To Dos appear on their assigned dates, not again on Today just because they are overdue. Gantt task bands use their real inclusive calendar-day spans; milestones use their own date. Project colors match the To Do project tags.
  • Navigation: The single-row toolbar shows the month or week range between previous/next arrows, a Month / Week dropdown and Today. Go to date is in Settings. Selecting a date opens its complete day agenda. Crowded days offer +N more; long bands continue across week boundaries.
  • Settings: The sliders beside Today open a popover with layers, Project / tagged To Dos, Gantt task levels (All, Main, or Actionable tasks without children), and Show completed work. Click outside or press Escape to close it. Standalone events are independent of project/completion filters. Calendar display preferences are browser-local, remembered separately per profile, and do not create GitHub commits.
  • Add a To Do: Select its date, then + To Do in the day agenda. The shared editor pre-fills the date and offers text, reminder time, project/task linking and rich-text notes. An unsaved add-item draft in To Do is kept separate. Existing items open the same editor; its Date field moves the item without rescheduling Gantt.
  • Edit Gantt: Click a task band or its day-agenda entry to edit the actual source task's name, start, calendar duration, milestone status, progress and notes. Parent dates remain derived from subtasks. A parent progress value is a manual override; leave it blank to return to automatic calculation. Linked completion keeps its existing rules and impact messages. Text, notes and dates of copied To Dos remain independent.
  • Events: Select a date and + Event for OOO, a birthday or other schedule information. Set a title, start/end dates (both included), and optional notes. Click an event to edit it; Delete asks for confirmation. Events have no checkbox and never move project dates or change working days.
  • Phones: The toolbar stays one row with a shortened date label; Month / Week moves into Settings > View. Month uses finger-sized dates, item counts and thin colored span strips; tap a date for full names and editing in its agenda. Week keeps readable bands and To Dos: swipe its grid sideways to see all seven days. The rest of the page does not scroll sideways. Settings scroll internally when needed, and rotation preserves open editor text.

Events are saved with their profile through browser saving, private GitHub sync, enabled local JSON writing, backups/import and Recovery. Pause sync also pauses event uploads, not local saving. Existing task/To Do PDF, image and .ics exports keep their existing scopes; Calendar itself does not add another export service.

Update the tracker on other devices/tabs before saving calendar events. Events use protected profile/cache format 3; older apps refuse it rather than silently dropping events. Previously saved projects and To Dos are retained. Replace the website's index.html and reload online on each device; the worker is unchanged. Do not clear site data.

7. To Do List

Click To Do in the sidebar for a day-by-day checklist. Ordinary items and project tags are independent of Gantt progress. Items linked to a specific Gantt task share completion with it; text, notes and dates stay independently editable.

Copy Gantt Tasks to To Do

  • Open: Click the project title, then Copy to To Do. On phones, tap the project title or its project-actions button and choose Copy to To Do. Gantt and Summary use the same project data.
  • Which tasks: Choose Tasks without children (the default, including standalone main tasks), Main tasks only, or All tasks, flattened. Folded tasks are included. Completed Gantt tasks are skipped; To Dos do not acquire a subtask hierarchy.
  • When: Put everything on one editable date, defaulting to Today, or use each task's own Gantt finish date, not the project's overall finish. Finish dates include the final calendar day, regardless of Working days display; zero-duration milestones use their own date. Past dates stay in the past and can appear Overdue.
  • What is copied: Task names, rich-text notes, the chosen destination date and project/task links. Gantt duration and hierarchy remain in Gantt. No Gantt task is removed or rescheduled. Later text, notes or date edits affect only the edited item; changing a schedule does not move previously copied To Dos.
  • Safe repeats: A preview counts items to add, already present and completed tasks skipped. Another copy of the same source task on the same day is skipped, including a renamed or unlinked original copy; existing text and completion are never overwritten by copying. Another day is allowed. Moving or deleting a copy leaves no permanent blacklist: copying again can recreate it on a now-empty date.

Task Links and Shared Completion

  • Link a manual item: Select a Project, then the optional Gantt task when adding an item. Or open Edit Item to add, change or remove its task link. A project tag alone never changes Gantt progress. New linked items start with the task's current completion. When linking an existing item with a different completion state, explicitly choose Keep Gantt or Use this To Do; nothing is changed until saved.
  • Completion: Completing a linked To Do sets its source task to 100%. Setting Gantt progress to 100% completes every To Do currently linked to that task, on every date in this profile. Lowering its progress reopens those linked copies. Copied names, notes and dates remain independent. If subtask progress automatically completes or reopens a parent, an in-app message names the affected parents and counts their linked To Dos.
  • Uncheck: Immediately restore the source task's previous percentage, or 0% if no earlier percentage was recorded. Only that task reopens; its descendants keep their current progress. Parents use a manual override so restored progress is not immediately replaced by their children. An in-app message explains the restored progress; no completion/reopening confirmation is needed.
  • Unlink: Choose No task link and save. This stops future completion updates without undoing previous Gantt progress or changing the To Do's current completion. Changing a linked item's project also requires removing its old task link. Deleting a To Do never deletes or reopens its Gantt task.
  • Delete a Gantt task/project: The confirmation counts the linked To Dos that will be kept and unlinked. Their text, notes, dates and completion are retained. Links are profile-local and use task identity, not matching names.

Completing a Linked Parent

Completing or reopening a linked parent happens immediately, without confirmation, from its checkbox, a reminder or a saved Edit. A non-blocking Progress updated message reports what changed and what was left unchanged. Coverage counts all nesting levels and currently linked To Dos on any date in this profile, including completed copies:

Linked descendantsImmediate action
None or someOverride only the parent to 100% using manual progress. The message counts descendants that remain unchanged, including those already complete; their progress and linked To Dos are not completed by this action.
All descendantsComplete the parent and its entire descendant branch to 100%, including their linked To Dos on every date. The message distinguishes descendants newly completed from those already complete.

Normal automatic ancestors can recalculate from changed child progress. A manual parent override stays in effect until you clear that parent's percentage in Gantt to return to automatic calculation. Unchecking a parent does not undo a previous whole-branch completion. Deletion/replacement confirmations and real choices about conflicting versions or link completion remain unchanged.

Update the tracker on other devices/tabs before using task links or To Do notes. These and remembered completion percentages require profile/cache format 2 or later; calendar events use format 3. GitHub, JSON writing, backups and Recovery retain this metadata. Older apps refuse the newer format rather than silently dropping links/events. Reload the updated application online; do not clear site data. No additional service or login is needed.

Export: In To Do view, use Backups > Export PDF report or Backups > Export image, below the same separator used for project exports. Both include the selected day and the Overdue section, with completed items, reminder times, project/task labels and saved notes, but without editing controls or navigation. This is not an all-dates export; unsaved add-item text is not included. Calendar .ics exports below remain available.

Adding & Completing Items

  • Add: Type in the box at the bottom and press Enter. The cursor stays put so you can add several items in a row.
  • Complete: Tick the checkbox. The item is struck through but stays where it is in the list.
  • Edit: Click an item's text to open Edit Item for wording, time, project, optional task link and independently editable rich-text Notes. In the wording box, press Enter to save or Shift+Enter for a new line; Enter in Notes adds a line. Use Esc or click outside to cancel. Hover and click the trash icon to delete it.
  • Reorder: Drag an item by the ⋮⋮ grip on its left and drop it on another item to change the order.

Times & Reminders

  • Every item has a time box. When empty it takes no space at all—hover the row and the full control strip appears, with the text re-wrapping around it. You can set or clear the time at any point, not just when creating the item.
  • Setting a time turns the item into a reminder. Clearing the box removes the reminder. Once a timed item is past due its time badge turns red.
  • The To Do sidebar entry shows a live badge counting outstanding items (red if anything is overdue), and the browser tab title shows the same count.
  • When a reminder comes due you get a popup that stays on screen until you deal with it, with three buttons: Snooze 10m, Done, and Dismiss. Changing an item's time re-arms it and cancels any snooze.
  • If several reminders are due at once—for example after the laptop wakes from sleep—they are collected into a single grouped catch-up popup instead of stacking up.
  • While a reminder is waiting, the browser tab title flashes so you notice it even from another tab.
  • A short chime plays with each reminder. Use the speaker icon in the To Do header to mute or unmute it; the choice is remembered.
  • If your browser has already been granted notification permission for this page, reminders also fire as desktop notifications. Otherwise you simply get the on-screen popup. Permission is asked for at most once, ever—if you decline or ignore it, you will never be prompted again.
  • Daily wrap-up: the Wrap-up time box in the header (default 6:00 PM) gives you one reminder listing everything still open—today's unfinished items plus anything overdue—regardless of whether those items have their own time. It fires once a day; if the page was closed at that hour you get it the next time you open the file. Clear the box to switch it off.
  • Note: Because this is a standalone HTML file, reminders can only fire while the page is open in a tab. For anything you must not miss, export it to your calendar (below).

Sending Reminders to Outlook / Google Calendar

  • Hover a timed item and click the calendar-export icon to download a .ics file for it. Open the file and your calendar app will offer to add the event.
  • Use Export .ics next to the day's title to download every timed item for that day in one file.
  • Events are created at the item's time with a 30 minute duration and a 10 minute advance alarm. Untimed items become all-day events with no alarm.
  • Saved notes and the current linked-task name, if any, are included in the event description. External calendar events do not acquire a live completion link back to Gantt.
  • Re-exporting the same item updates the existing calendar entry rather than creating a duplicate.
  • Important: this is a one-way copy, not a live sync. Editing or deleting the item here does not change an event you already added to your calendar—re-export it, or delete it in the calendar yourself.

Dates, Copying & Overdue Items

  • Use the ‹ / › arrows or the date picker to move between days, and the Today button to jump back.
  • Move to tomorrow: hover an item and click the →| arrow to push it to the next day in one click. Click it again on the new day to keep pushing it forward.
  • Move to a date: click the calendar icon and pick any day. The item leaves the current day and lands on the one you chose, keeping its time, project tag and text.
  • Copy to a date: click the duplicate icon to place a copy on another day while leaving the original where it is. Notes and task links are retained. Linked copies share the task's completion; ordinary copies start open. An existing copy of the same linked source on the destination day is kept unchanged.
  • Anything left unfinished on a past date is collected into a red Overdue panel at the top, with all of its controls permanently on show. Click → Today to carry an item forward.
  • If the next day already has unfinished items, a small Next Day line appears at the bottom—click it to jump there. It is always relative to the day you are looking at, and stays hidden when that day is empty.

Project Tags

  • Optionally tag an item to a project using the dropdown next to the add box.
  • Every item also carries its own tag dropdown, revealed when you hover the row, so you can change or remove the project at any time—including on items that were created without one. Once set, the project shows as a small colored badge on the right.
  • When an item is tagged, an open icon appears on hover next to the tag to jump straight to that project.
  • Tagging is entirely optional—leave it on "No project" for general items. A specific task link is optional too. To keep the checklist uncluttered, no separate linked-task label is displayed. Hover the project tag for the linked task and its progress, or open Edit Item to inspect, change or remove the link. On touch screens, use Edit Item.

To Do items are saved with everything else—they are included in your LocalStorage, Live Auto-Save file, and JSON backups automatically.

8. Application Updates and Offline Access

Online page loads try the latest published application and update its offline copy. If the page cannot be downloaded, the last cached application is used. Already open tabs keep their current application code until reloaded; GitHub data checks are independent of this. Routine interface releases can update only index.html after the stable worker has been installed. A changed worker may show Update ready; finish syncing before activating it. Never clear site data just to update, because that removes unsynced work and local recovery.

Add event

All-day information for this profile, not a task to complete. OOO and other events do not reschedule Gantt tasks.

Edit Item

Notes

In the wording box: Enter saves, Shift+Enter adds a line. In Notes: Enter adds a line. Esc cancels.

Copy to To Do

Copy task names and notes into a flat checklist, keeping the Gantt intact. Only completion stays linked; text, notes and dates can be edited independently. Completed tasks are skipped.

Includes standalone main tasks and folded tasks. Existing copies of the same source task on the same day are kept unchanged. Past finish dates stay in the past and can appear Overdue. Linked parent completion applies immediately and reports its impact without confirmation.
